intent_en: To demonstrate that private school participation in Britain is heavily concentrated among the highest income earners.
previous_intent: To explain the dominance of the wealthy in private school intakes in Britain by illustrating the sharp increase in participation among the highest income earners alongside cuts to state school funding.
narration_support: which is why intakes are dominated by the very wealthy.
chart_support: Line chart plotting participation rate against income percentiles, showing a flat trend for lower incomes and a sharp vertical increase for the top income bracket.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states that intakes are dominated by the wealthy, which is visually confirmed by the chart showing a dramatic spike in participation rate only at the highest income percentiles (labeled as the richest group).
